=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: radical-reinterpretation (probability 0.05)
Title: Trailblazer Time Machine
Thesis: A Microsoft Copilot side-pane in Teams that renders the semester-by-semester arc of an alumna who started exactly where the first-year sits today.
Why this frame: The deepest first-year pain isn't lack of mentors — it's the absence of a mental model for what a five-year arc even looks like. Reframing the alumni network as a longitudinal decision-dataset (not a mentor roster) lets students interrogate trajectories before they interrogate people.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Aisha Okonkwo
  Role: First-year undeclared undergraduate, College of Arts Media & Design pathway curious
  Context: Eight weeks into her first semester at Northeastern. Has opened NUworks twice, felt overwhelmed by 4,200 co-op postings, and closed it. Lives inside Microsoft Teams for group projects and Canvas for coursework. Asks her RA versions of the same question every week: 'what does someone like me actually do after sophomore year?'
  Emotional state: Curious but quietly anxious. Performs confidence in class. Privately worries that classmates with declared majors have a roadmap she missed.
  Pain points:
    - Cannot picture a five-year arc — co-op, classes, lateral pivots feel like a fog she has to walk into blind
    - Intimidated by formal networking; the idea of cold-emailing an alum is paralyzing
    - Brand-name hyper-fixation in her peer group (FAANG, McKinsey) crowds out lateral or creative paths she might actually love
    - Existing tools (NU Source, NUworks) require leaving Teams and learning a new interface, so she abandons them
  JTBD: When I'm worried I'm falling behind a roadmap I can't see, I want to glimpse the actual trajectories of people who started where I am, so I can choose my next semester with intention instead of anxiety.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Alumni Trailblazer (opt-in donor of trajectory data): Submits anonymized arc to SharePoint; receives ping when a first-year invites a chat after exploring their (anonymized) path
  - Alumni Relations Lead: Curates and validates the SharePoint trajectory list; enforces k-anonymity thresholds before any arc is rendered
  - Strategic Co-op Director: Reviews aggregate exploration patterns in Power BI to identify which arcs first-years cluster around and where the curriculum gap sits
  - Academic Technology Advocate (Jen's team): Owns the Copilot extension manifest, Power Automate flow, and Graph API provisioning
  - FERPA Compliance Officer: Audits the k-threshold and anonymization rules quarterly; their seal appears in the side-pane footer

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Aisha opens Copilot inside the Teams desktop client, types 'show me someone who started undeclared and ended up in product design,' and watches the side-pane render three real anonymized five-year arcs — semester-by-semester courses, co-ops, decision forks. She clicks fork #2 of the second arc, sees the alternate path the alumna almost took, and taps 'Invite this Trailblazer to a 15-minute chat.' Power Automate drafts the introduction; she sends it. Total elapsed time: ninety seconds.

USE CASES (11) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Trajectory Search in Copilot Side-Pane
     Trigger: Aisha opens the Copilot pane in Teams and types a natural-language query like 'undeclared to product design' or 'started in biology, ended up in climate policy.'
     Flow: She invokes Copilot with the keyboard shortcut → the Trailblazer Time Machine extension is suggested as a skill → she confirms → Copilot routes the query to a Power Automate flow that retrieves matching anonymized trajectories from the alumni SharePoint list → three arcs render in the side-pane within two seconds.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro parses the natural-language query into structured filters (start state, end state, optional industry); Wiki RAG retrieves the matching trajectory records.
     Outcome: Aisha now has three concrete five-year arcs to interrogate — no portal switch, no form, no login.
  2. Anonymized Five-Year Arc Visualization
     Trigger: Aisha clicks one of the three returned arcs to expand it.
     Flow: The pane unfurls a horizontal timeline split into ten semester nodes → each node shows course themes, co-op employer category (not name unless k≥5), and a one-line decision summary → the FERPA k-anonymity badge stays visible in the footer.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 generates the one-line decision summary per node; the anonymization filter strips any field where the cohort size drops below k=5.
     Outcome: For the first time, Aisha sees the SHAPE of a career arc — not advice, not a brand name, but a trajectory.
  3. Decision Fork Drill-Down
     Trigger: Aisha taps a fork icon between Semester 4 and Semester 5 — the moment the alumna pivoted from graphic design to product design.
     Flow: The pane reveals a drill-down card → 'At this point, she had two co-op offers: branding agency vs. fintech UX team. She chose fintech because…' → three to four sentences of synthesized narrative → an 'explore the road not taken' counterfactual button appears.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 synthesizes the decision-point narrative from the alumna's structured trajectory record plus her optional reflection text.
     Outcome: Aisha understands not just what happened, but WHY — and that decisions, not destinies, shape arcs.
  4. Counterfactual 'What If She Had Picked Differently'
     Trigger: Aisha taps 'explore the road not taken' on a fork.
     Flow: The pane splits into a two-column comparison → left: actual arc continued → right: AI-synthesized plausible alternative arc drawn from OTHER alumni who took the rejected fork → a banner clearly labels the right column 'Synthesized from 14 similar alumni — not a single real person.'
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro composes the counterfactual by aggregating downstream patterns of alumni who took the unchosen path; Verbalized Sampling produces three variant counterfactuals so Aisha sees a distribution, not one prediction.
     Outcome: Aisha learns that any single fork has a probabilistic fan of futures, defusing the brand-name hyper-fixation.
  5. Invite the Trailblazer to a 15-Minute Chat
     Trigger: After exploring an arc, Aisha taps 'invite this Trailblazer.'
     Flow: Copilot drafts a personalized introduction citing the specific decision fork Aisha found compelling → she edits or accepts → Power Automate creates a private Teams group chat between Aisha and the alumna → bot posts an icebreaker prompt and a suggested 15-minute agenda → email fallback fires if the alum doesn't open Teams in 48 hours.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 drafts the introduction; Graph API provisions the chat; Power Automate runs the fallback logic.
     Outcome: Friction-free introduction grounded in something specific — not 'tell me about your career' but 'why did you pick fintech over branding in Spring 2021?'
  6. Save Trajectory to a Canvas Notebook
     Trigger: Aisha hits the bookmark icon on an arc.
     Flow: The arc serializes as a structured markdown card → posts into her private Canvas 'Co-op Compass' notebook (a hidden CLR-tagged module) → a toast confirms 'Saved to your Co-op Compass — revisit anytime.'
     AI role: Power Automate writes to Canvas via the LTI bridge; CLR tagging happens silently per Liz's stealth-implementation guardrail.
     Outcome: Aisha builds a personal library of trajectories she can revisit; the CLR ledger silently captures her exploration as evidence of self-directed career inquiry.
  7. FERPA-Safe k-Anonymity Aggregation
     Trigger: Aisha runs a very narrow query that would surface fewer than 5 alumni.
     Flow: Instead of returning identifiable arcs, the pane shows a graceful empty state → 'Only 2 Trailblazers match this exact path — to protect their privacy, we'll show you the broader pattern instead' → renders an aggregated heatmap of related arcs.
     AI role: Pre-retrieval guard checks cohort size; if k<5, falls back to aggregated visualization rendered by Gemini.
     Outcome: Aisha trusts the system; alumni privacy is visibly honored; FERPA compliance is in-product chrome, not buried in a policy doc.
  8. CLR Stealth Tagging of Explored Paths
     Trigger: Every arc Aisha opens, every fork she drills into, every Trailblazer she invites.
     Flow: Power Automate writes a structured event to the SharePoint CLR ledger → the event is invisible to Aisha → over time it builds a comprehensive Co-op Learning Record without ever using the acronym 'CLR' in the UI.
     AI role: Rule-based event capture; no model needed.
     Outcome: Liz's stealth-CLR mandate is met. By spring, advisors can see Aisha has explored 14 trajectories across 3 industries — without Aisha ever 'using a CLR tool.'
  9. Power BI Insight Loop for Strategic Co-op Director
     Trigger: Weekly cohort review meeting.
     Flow: Director opens a Power BI dashboard embedded in Teams → sees most-explored trajectories, fork patterns, queries that returned k<5 → identifies curricular gaps (e.g. 'too few alumni arcs into climate tech to render').
     AI role: Gemini summarizes weekly exploration patterns into a 3-bullet director's brief.
     Outcome: The product becomes an institutional sensor for unmet career curiosity.
  10. Verbalized Sampling on Arc Variants
     Trigger: When a query has many matching alumni, the system could pick one or three — Aisha sees three.
     Flow: Behind the scenes, the model generates 5 candidate arcs at varied probabilities → returns top 3 spanning the distribution → labels them 'most common path,' 'mid-frequency path,' 'rare but possible.'
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro with Verbalized Sampling prompt; each arc shows its probability badge.
     Outcome: Aisha sees that 'undeclared to product design' has a common road and rare ones — defeating roadmap-anxiety with statistical honesty.
  11. Conversation Resumption with Prior Trailblazer
     Trigger: Aisha returns to Copilot weeks later after her first chat.
     Flow: Copilot greets her with 'Your last chat with a Trailblazer touched on prototyping skills. Want to see arcs that emphasized that?' → suggests three new trajectories.
     AI role: Embeddings over her prior chat transcripts (with consent) seed a follow-on retrieval query.
     Outcome: The product feels like it remembers her — a longitudinal companion, not a one-shot tool.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Copilot Trajectory Search Pane — purpose: Entry point. A right-docked Copilot side-pane in Teams where Aisha types her natural-language trajectory query.
     Primary element: A single input field with placeholder 'show me someone who started…' plus suggested chips ('undeclared → product design', 'biology → climate policy', 'business → film').
     Motion character: The pane slides in from the right edge over 280ms with a soft easing; the placeholder text gently cycles through 3 example queries every 4 seconds.
  2. Three-Arc Result Strip — purpose: Displays the three Verbalized-Sampled trajectories returned for the query, each as a horizontal compressed timeline with a probability badge.
     Primary element: Three stacked horizontal timeline cards labeled 'most common,' 'mid-frequency,' 'rare but possible' with course/co-op/decision dots along each.
     Motion character: Cards render one after another at 120ms intervals; dots populate left-to-right like a chart drawing itself, evoking a journey unfolding.
  3. Five-Year Arc Expanded View — purpose: Full unfurled trajectory with 10 semester nodes, fork icons at decision points, and the FERPA badge in the footer.
     Primary element: A cartographic timeline rendered with subtle topographic shading — semesters as nodes, co-ops as larger waypoints, forks as glowing diamond markers.
     Motion character: Nodes pulse softly when interactive; hovering a node reveals a tooltip; the entire view supports horizontal scroll with elastic momentum.
  4. Decision Fork Drill-Down Card — purpose: Reveals why an alumna made a specific decision and offers the counterfactual exploration button.
     Primary element: A vertically-stacked card with: fork title, 3-sentence synthesized narrative, the two options she weighed, and a 'road not taken' CTA.
     Motion character: The card slides up from the fork marker over 220ms; text fades in line-by-line at 60ms cadence for a reading-pace reveal.
  5. Counterfactual Comparison View — purpose: Side-by-side comparison of the actual arc continuation vs. an AI-synthesized alternative arc.
     Primary element: Two parallel mini-timelines under a clearly-labeled 'Synthesized from N alumni — not a real person' banner.
     Motion character: Both timelines draw simultaneously; the synthesized side has a subtle dashed-line texture to visually distinguish it from real data.
  6. Invite-to-Chat CTA Sheet — purpose: Lets Aisha edit and send the Copilot-drafted introduction to the Trailblazer behind an arc.
     Primary element: A pre-filled message draft citing the specific decision fork that drew her in, with edit/send buttons and a small preview of the resulting Teams group chat header.
     Motion character: The sheet rises from the bottom of the pane; the message text shimmers in via a typewriter-stagger for the first 600ms to signal AI authorship.
  7. Canvas Notebook Save Confirmation — purpose: Confirms the arc has been saved to Aisha's private Co-op Compass notebook in Canvas.
     Primary element: A small toast at the bottom of the pane with 'Saved to your Co-op Compass' and a link 'view in Canvas.'
     Motion character: Toast fades in over 180ms, holds for 3 seconds, fades out — non-intrusive.
  8. k-Anonymity Empty State — purpose: Graceful fallback when fewer than 5 alumni match a narrow query.
     Primary element: A short empathetic message plus an aggregated heatmap of adjacent trajectories.
     Motion character: The heatmap renders with a gentle diffusion bloom, signaling aggregate-not-individual.
  9. Director's Power BI Insight Tab — purpose: Behind-the-scenes view for the Strategic Co-op Director showing aggregate exploration patterns.
     Primary element: A Power BI report embedded as a Teams tab with three KPI cards (queries this week, top explored arcs, gaps where k<5).
     Motion character: Charts animate in with the standard Power BI bar-grow; the gap-detection card pulses amber when new gaps emerge.
  10. Returning-User Welcome Pane — purpose: What Aisha sees on her second, fifth, fifteenth visit — a longitudinal companion view.
     Primary element: A short greeting referencing her last exploration, three suggested next arcs, and a small 'your Co-op Compass has 8 saved trajectories' chip.
     Motion character: The greeting fades in with a gentle 300ms ease; the saved-count chip counts up from 0 to its value.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Trajectory Pattern Retrieval
     User action: Aisha types a natural-language query into the Copilot pane.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Free-text query plus a structured SharePoint list of opt-in alumni trajectory records (start_major, end_role, semester_nodes, co_op_employers, reflection_text).
     Output: A ranked list of matching anonymized trajectory record IDs with similarity scores.
     User benefit: Aisha asks in plain English and gets matching real arcs in under two seconds — no portal, no form.
  2. Decision-Point Narrative Synthesis
     User action: Aisha taps a fork on a timeline.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The alumna's structured fork record (two options, chosen option, optional reflection text) plus her broader trajectory context.
     Output: A 3-sentence narrative explaining the decision in the alumna's implied voice without quoting her verbatim.
     User benefit: Aisha sees the WHY behind a decision, not just the WHAT — building real intuition about how arcs are made.
  3. Counterfactual Path Generation with Verbalized Sampling
     User action: Aisha taps 'explore the road not taken' on a fork.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: The unchosen option at the fork plus a cohort of alumni who DID take that option.
     Output: Three plausible alternative arc continuations, each with a probability label ('common outcome,' 'mid-frequency,' 'rare').
     User benefit: Aisha sees that any decision fans into a distribution of futures, not one fate — defusing roadmap-anxiety.
  4. k-Anonymity FERPA Guard
     User action: Every query Aisha runs, every arc that renders.
     Model: Rule-based pre-filter + Embeddings for cohort similarity
     Input: Query result set, cohort size, sensitivity classification of each field.
     Output: Either: pass-through with full arc, OR: aggregated heatmap fallback when k<5.
     User benefit: Aisha sees FERPA compliance as a visible feature, not a hidden policy — and trusts the system more for it.
  5. Personalized Introduction Drafting
     User action: Aisha taps 'invite this Trailblazer.'
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Aisha's profile context (year, college, declared interests) plus the specific fork or moment she found compelling on the arc.
     Output: A 4-5 sentence personalized introduction message draft, citing the specific arc moment.
     User benefit: Aisha sends a specific, thoughtful intro instead of 'tell me about your career' — dramatically lifting alum response rates.
  6. Headline Aha — Arc Variant Verbalized Sampling
     User action: Aisha submits her natural-language trajectory query.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: All matching trajectory records for the query.
     Output: Three sampled arcs spanning the probability distribution — most common, mid-frequency, rare-but-possible — each rendered with its own probability badge.
     User benefit: Instead of one prescriptive 'this is your path,' Aisha sees the SHAPE of what's possible — the headline emotional moment of the entire product.
  7. Returning-User Memory & Suggestion
     User action: Aisha opens the Copilot pane on a return visit.
     Model: Embeddings + Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Her prior queries, saved arcs, chats she initiated, forks she lingered on.
     Output: A short greeting plus three suggested next arcs to explore.
     User benefit: The product feels like a companion that remembers — not a stateless tool.
  8. Director's Weekly Brief Synthesis
     User action: Strategic Co-op Director opens the Power BI tab on Monday.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Weekly aggregate exploration events from the SharePoint ledger.
     Output: A 3-bullet executive brief: top explored arcs, top unmet query patterns, top emerging curricular gaps.
     User benefit: The director gets a sensor on first-year career curiosity that no other tool provides.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Cartographic timeline elegance — topographic line work, restrained editorial typography, generous negative space, a single warm accent for decision forks against a cool slate palette. Narrative-rich but data-grounded. Quietly profound, never showy.
  Hero treatment: The five-year arc is the hero — rendered as a horizontal cartographic timeline with subtle elevation shading, where each semester is a node, each co-op is a larger waypoint, and each decision fork is a glowing amber diamond. The timeline scrolls horizontally with elastic momentum, and probability badges sit in the upper-right of each arc card like a wine vintage label. The Microsoft Copilot purple gradient frames the side-pane chrome to keep the host-app identity honest.
  Motion character: Considered, deliberate, breath-paced. Nothing snaps. Slide-ins use 220-320ms ease-out curves. Text fades line-by-line at reading pace. Loading states shimmer rather than spin. Decision-fork interactions pulse once like a heartbeat — to honor the weight of choice.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Cartographic-style hero illustration for the empty-state pane: an abstract topographic map where contour lines transform into a multi-branching timeline, in slate blue with amber fork markers, editorial restraint
    2. Anonymized alumni avatar placeholders: muted gradient circles with abstracted silhouettes — no identifiable features — in a watercolor diffusion style that reads as 'a person, anonymized'
    3. Marketing hero for first-year onboarding email: a single first-year student at a desk looking at a Teams pane that shows three branching paths extending into a horizon, photographic style, natural window light
    4. Visual metaphor for the counterfactual comparison view: two parallel rivers in a topographic map, one solid line and one dashed, joining and diverging — abstract, no human figures
    5. Director's dashboard hero: an aerial-view abstract of a city of intersecting trajectories rendered as light trails, dark mode, editorial data-visualization aesthetic
    6. FERPA-safe empty state illustration: a soft diffusion bloom of overlapping circles, suggesting aggregation without identification, in pale slate

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a longitudinal companion analyzing a student's past queries and saved arcs to generate a personalized greeting and 3 suggested next arcs.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student context: {student_profile}. Past queries: {past_queries}. Saved arcs: {saved_arcs}. Generate a short greeting referencing their last exploration and suggest 3 new trajectory queries.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You parse natural language career queries into structured filters and retrieve matching anonymized trajectory records from the SharePoint list.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Query: '{user_query}'. Available trajectories: {sharepoint_list}. Return the top matching trajectory IDs.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a strict privacy filter. You check the cohort size of retrieved trajectories. If k<5, you block passthrough and trigger the aggregate fallback.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Retrieved cohort size: {cohort_size}. Evaluate against k=5 threshold.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You analyze a cohort of matching trajectories and select 3 that span the probability distribution to show the user a range of outcomes.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Matched trajectories: {matched_trajectories}. Select 3 variants and label them 'most common', 'mid-frequency', and 'rare but possible'.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You synthesize a 3-sentence narrative explaining why an alumna chose one path over another at a decision fork, using their implied voice without quoting verbatim.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Fork context: {fork_data}. Alumna reflection: {reflection_text}. Synthesize the 'why' behind this decision.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You generate a plausible alternative career arc by aggregating downstream patterns of other alumni who took the unchosen path at a specific fork.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Unchosen option: {rejected_option}. Cohort who took this option: {counterfactual_cohort}. Generate a synthesized 5-semester continuation.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You draft a personalized, 4-5 sentence Teams introduction message from a first-year student to an alum, specifically citing the decision fork the student found compelling.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student profile: {student_profile}. Alum trajectory: {trajectory_id}. Compelling fork: {fork_details}. Draft the intro.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You analyze weekly aggregate exploration events from the CLR ledger and synthesize a 3-bullet executive brief for the Strategic Co-op Director.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Weekly events: {clr_ledger_events}. Identify top explored arcs, unmet query patterns, and emerging curricular gaps.

critique.summary: The prototype achieves 66% session coverage. While the core visual timeline and multi-provider AI proxy are well-implemented, it misses two critical AI fetch calls (trajectory retrieval and counterfactual generation) and fails to persist CLR events to sessionStorage as required by the stealth instrumentation spec. FERPA badges are also missing from the result screens.
